editorial.headline: A Painting Trade That Cannot Be Registered as PMA in Bali
editorial.standfirst: A foreigner cannot register this nationally open painting-retail activity as PMA in Bali today.
editorial.body:
At its core, this activity is the retail trade in paintings: portraits, animal paintings and landscapes, together with art-gallery activity when the gallery sells paintings. The definition is deliberately commercial. It concerns the point at which paintings are presented to buyers and sold through a retail operation or a selling gallery, rather than the creation of the work itself. The named examples illustrate the category’s range without changing its centre of gravity: the business is the sale of paintings, and a gallery belongs within it when sales are part of that activity. Whether the paintings are portraits, animals or landscapes, the record treats them as objects of retail sale; the gallery reference is equally specific about sales.

The registration picture is broad at the national level. The record opens the activity to micro, small, medium and large businesses; it does not reserve the trade for one particular operating scale. Its PMA status is open, and its national foreign-ownership ceiling is 100%. That is a full-ownership ceiling, stated on the national basis of Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. That scale range captures both the smallest listed form and the largest without changing the national PMA conclusion recorded for the activity. A foreign investor assessing a retail painting business or an art gallery that sells paintings can therefore read the national position plainly: the activity is available across the listed scales and national rules permit foreign ownership up to 100%.

Bali supplies the decisive qualification. This activity is blocked for PMA registration there, with the record identifying the issue as a risk-class block. At the large scale, OSS risk is Low or Medium-Low across every scope. That result triggers Bali’s island-wide, permanent moratorium on PMA for the activity, dated 13 May 2026. That finding is not an optional caution or an administrative footnote; it determines the local PMA outcome even though the national record remains open. National openness does not create a Bali PMA registration route for this activity. The contrast is not a smaller Bali foreign-ownership ceiling: the Bali record states a block. A proposal that fits the national scope—retailing paintings, including a gallery’s sale of them—must therefore keep the two jurisdictions in view: full foreign ownership is nationally permitted to the stated ceiling, while Bali’s moratorium prevents PMA registration for the same activity.
editorial.pullQuote: National openness does not create a Bali PMA registration route for this activity.
